figures.caption: Fig. 1: Overview of AcrossDEX 1.0. (a) Human pretraining and robot expert data support adaptation with human replay. (b) A shared Transformer processes images and motion history. Masks select human or robot finger fields. Each method, task, and hand uses a separately trained policy. (c) The robot policy predicts 60 commands, executes the first $K$ steps, and updates its history. Blue, green, and orange denote shared, human, and robot components. Gray fields are masked.
Fig. 2: Success rates for lid opening and return and object reorientation with two hand embodiments. Each configuration is post-trained separately and evaluated using ( 11 ).

Fig. 3: A successful closed-loop opening and return trajectory with Inspire hands and Flow. The frontal views show the initial state, contact interaction, full opening, and the final state after lid return.
Fig. 4: Successful closed-loop reorientation. Top: Inspire with BC. Bottom: Allegro with Flow. Columns correspond to $0$ , $0.22$ , $0.43$ , and $0.67\,$ s.
